i226-lm.note: The only port with AMT. A host OS that bridges it or changes its MAC kills out-of-band access without touching anything that looks related.

i226-v.note: No AMT. Identical-looking socket next to the one that has it.

sfp28-1.note: Ubuntu names it for the X710's second function, and sfp28-2 for its first: LLDP on the ToRs showed ber1-edge's and ber1-svc's sfp28-1 DACs arriving from enp2s0f1np1 (2026-09-24).

appliance.note: A KVM, a PDU or a transfer-switch card: one network port, and management is all it does.

mgmt.note: Its only port, so unlike an MS-01 there is no identical socket next to it to get wrong.

mac-mini.note: Apple silicon has no BMC and no AMT, so this hardware has no out-of-band network path at all. Recovery is a PDU outlet cycle plus `pmset autorestart 1`, and its console is a crash-cart KVM wheeled to the box rather than a permanent link. That is why it declares no out-of-band interface: the absence is the fact, and it is what makes the switched PDU a recovery dependency rather than a convenience.

en0.note: Its only NIC, so a mini lands on exactly one ToR.

eats16n.note: 1U, 2x C20 in, 8x C13 plus 1x C19 out, 16A/3.84kW, 8 ms transfer. Networking is built in (Netpack), so both inputs can be monitored over SNMP.

netpack.note: Built-in management network port. Eaton's Netpack, not an add-in card.

evmafc20a.note: Switched zero-U PDU. Speaks Modbus TCP, a REST API, SNMP, LDAP and HTTPS; the REST API is what a power driver should target. This is the remote-power path the Mac fleet's recovery model depends on, because a mini has no out-of-band of its own.

usb.note: Feeds an RS485 sensor chain through a USB converter, and powers it.

emp-gen2.note: No Ethernet at all. It hangs off a PDU's USB port through a USB-to-RS485 converter and draws its power over that link, so it occupies no switch port and has no management link. Its identity on the bus is a Modbus address, not a NIC.
